## 2. What to build

**§9 Catch up** (prototype frame 1)
- **One list of what's addressed to you**, grouped by conversation (newest first is a Display option): direct messages, `@you` and `@Team`, replies in chains you're in and to your own messages, announcements, a conversation set to "Every message" as one line ("Acme · 12 new", CH73), Remind me items when due, and quiet lines (added to or removed from a channel, the conversion's level reset). It's a mode: the bottom bar shows **Reply `R` · Done `Space` · Task `T` · Later `H` · Open `⏎` · More**, then "4 left · Esc"; the selected item opens on the right as the message in context (ten lines either side, "Open in conversation"). Keys on a grouped item act on its newest message.
- **Done** clears it; reading it in its conversation clears it too; **the bell and Catch up are one state** (a mention cleared in either is gone from both, CH38). **Later** brings it back at a time you pick (in 1 hour · this evening · tomorrow · pick); **Remind me** on any message does the same from its ⋯ (CH51); `/remind` in the composer reminds you about the conversation. The ⋯ offers "Done all in this conversation" with Undo.
- **Empty:** "You're caught up. Nothing is waiting for you. Three channels have messages you weren't asked about; they'll keep."
- **The rules behind the counts:** an `@you` in a conversation set to "Nothing" waits here silently, no ping, no count (CH40); when quiet hours, do not disturb, a vacation or Focus end, nothing pings and everything waits here (CH41).

**Edge cases this block handles** (§Edge cases)
- A reminder set on a message for next week → it returns to the top of Catch up at that time with one notice; "Remind me" beyond a year → refused.
- 300 items after a week away → Catch up stays grouped and fast; "Done all in this conversation" with Undo; Done on a group clears its messages' bell twins.

- **The bell draws chat excerpts in the stored form** (completes AC13.7; orchestrator's choice, deferred to by Maciej): a notice whose `payload.format_version = 2` renders its excerpt through the stored-form parser (`src/features/chat/markup-v2/`) as inline text, so a converted `moduo://person/<id>` shows the person's name, not the URI (today `src/features/spine/activity.ts` prints `p.excerpt` as text). CV-1 marks every chat excerpt with `format_version = 2`. Rejected: leaving it to CV-23's cleanup (old excerpts would show raw links until then).

## 3. Acceptance criteria

**AC2 — A hackathon team's weekend (the hackathon cut)**
- **AC2.5** after a sleep shift Catch up lists what was addressed to you, grouped, finishable with Space

**AC3 — A duo's week**
- **AC3.4** "Remind me tomorrow" on a message brings it back once

**AC5 — A PM's week**
- **AC5.4** "Later · this evening" on a Catch up item

**AC7 — Catch up and notifications**
- **AC7.3** "Every message" pings once per burst and lists one line per conversation
- **AC7.4** "Nothing" keeps `@you` in Catch up silently

**Tests that prove them** (file · name · AC · plain English)

- `supabase/tests/chat_later.test.sql` · "Later and Remind me" · proves AC3.4, AC5.4 · A reminder returns the item on time with one notice; `/remind` reminds about the conversation; beyond a year is refused.
- `tests/chat-catchup.spec.ts` · "the mode row and keys" · proves AC2.5, AC5.4, AC7.3 · R replies, Space clears, T opens the capture with the From chip, H offers Later, ⏎ opens the message in context; a grouped item acts on its newest message; "Done all in this conversation" undoes.

## 4. Decisions that bind it

- **Remind me and Later are one mechanism** (round-3 §2.16, #8): `chat_op_remind(message_id | channel_id, at)` snoozes the person's open Catch up item for that message, or creates one with reason `reminder` (any message, addressed to you or not); `at = null` clears; **horizon one year** (beyond is refused). `/remind` in the composer reminds about the conversation (`channel_id`, no message): it returns the conversation's newest message at that time. A job every minute, `chat__fire_later()` (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), brings due items back to the top of Catch up, sends one `chat_reminder` notice through CV-6a's gate and undismisses the bell twin. Schedule it like `20261013110000_notifications_v3.sql`. `remind`, like the other Catch up ops, skips the plan check (#25) and logs no activity row (#15).
- **Later's times** (#33): in 1 hour · this evening (18:00 in your zone) · tomorrow (9:00) · pick a time; the zone is Time & region's (`src/lib/time-region.ts`). Remind me is also in a message's ⋯ and on `H`.
- **The Catch up view** (§9, §16): a mode of the page, grouped by conversation (newest first is a Display option: `src/components/ui/display-menu.tsx`); the bottom bar's centre becomes the mode row through `src/components/app/bottom-bar-mode.ts` (six actions then More; "4 left · Esc"); the selected item opens on the right as the **message in context** (CV-8b's item, ten lines either side, "Open in conversation"); keys on a grouped item act on its newest message; ↑↓ move between items; Esc leaves. "Done all in this conversation" (⋯) with Undo through `chat_op_catchup_done` / `_reopen` (CV-5). Done on a group clears its messages' bell twins. 300 items after a week away stay grouped and fast.
- **Zero state** is the §9 line above (`EmptyState`); the Catch up row's count in the sidebar is CV-8a's.
- **Widget data** (§2.25 l): expose a read of the open Catch up items from the store for CV-22's Catch up widget; no widget here.

## 7. Watch out

- Time zones and midnight: "this evening" and "tomorrow" are in the person's zone, not the server's.
- An item snoozed with Later is hidden in Catch up **and** in the bell until it returns.
- **Tier 2** (migrations, RLS, contracts, moduo-mcp, src/lib/runtime*): one `/code-review high` and one security scan of the diff at the end; scan findings go only into the hand-back.
- **Migration:** stamp provisional (re-cut on apply day, chat's order kept); redefine from live bodies (`pg_get_functiondef`); re-state grants by name (`DROP` + `CREATE` resets them); re-assert the Realtime publication if you publish a table; apply only on your migration turn, then `bun run db:test chat`; never `local:reset` or `migration up` (runbook, `docs/gotchas/supabase.md`).
- **Hot files:** `src/features/chat/store/*` and `src/lib/runtime.chat.web.ts`. Keep edits there small; another builder may change them too.
- **Public repo:** describe no security weakness in any file; tell the orchestrator in the hand-back.

## 8. Out of scope for this block

The Catch up widget (CV-22); the OS and browser rings (CV-6b); the gate's quiet-hours rules and `held_at` (CV-18); Focus summary notices (CV-18); items of reason `added` and `removed` (CV-15).
